question: Does using covariates from the records' own period change the study's verdict?
why: 98.5% of the records postdate CHELSA's 1981-2010 climatology (median year 2021)

design.why_four: ERA5 monthly means carry no daily max/min temperature, so bio5 and bio6 cannot be built faithfully from them; the CHELSA baseline was rerun with the same four so only dataset and period differ

runs.chelsa4: CHELSA 1981-2010 (~1 km), the study's own data
runs.era5_1981-2010: ERA5 (~24 km box) over the same period: isolates dataset and support
runs.era5_2011-2025: ERA5 over the records' period: the time effect

design.why_not_climate_dt: Climate DT is a free-running projection under SSP3-7.0; its 2021 is a plausible 2021, not the observed one. ERA5 assimilates observations.

support_note: value of the source grid box containing the cell centre (~24 km)
verdict: unchanged: every run stays far outside the 47.8-68.6% reference range, so the study's Contradicted conclusion is robust to covariate support, dataset and period
caveats: museum strategy only, one depth (nside 256), four covariates
the effects measured (0.6 to 2.4 pp) are of the same order as the 0.57 pp reproduction gap between our baseline and the published number
closing the gap to the reference range would need about 28 pp
